own_solution.law: P = w/L - (sin(2 u2) - sin(2 u1))/(2 n pi), u = n pi x/L
assumptions: ideal probe responding only within the slice

defect_reasons.insufficient_boundary_condition: T3E63 does not say at which edge the slice is widened; the certified answers (0.350678, 0.359585, 0.476585) assume the right edge with the left edge fixed at 0.6 nm, but widening at the left edge or symmetrically gives different probabilities (q = 0.24: 0.4594 left, 0.4137 symmetric), so the answer is not unique.
defect_reasons.other: 'The coating ... is widened' is an odd way to say thickened, and the base text introduces 'a second chip' with no first chip mentioned; wording only.

counterexamples: T3E63, q = 0.24 nm added at the left edge (slice 0.36-1.50 nm): P = 0.5 - (0.12 - sin(0.48 pi)/(4 pi)) = 0.4594 vs certified 0.359585.
T3E63, q = 0.24 nm split equally (slice 0.48-1.62 nm): P = 0.5017 - 0.0880 = 0.4137 vs certified 0.359585.
notes: Verified certified answers under the right-edge reading: q=0.16 -> F(b)=0.55333 - sin(0.21333 pi)/(4 pi)=0.50390, P=0.35068; q=0.24 -> 0.35958; q=0.56 -> F(b)=0.68667 - sin(0.74667 pi)/(4 pi)=0.62981, P=0.47659. Base 0.346774 correct. D sentences correct. Change from pass 1: the declared minimal pairs are T1E15/T3E63 and TE83E/T6A0A, both of which are same-number variants differing only in attachment, so I withdraw my pass-1 rendering_not_minimal concern (I had guessed T3E63 paired with T6A0A). The T3E63 edge ambiguity remains and makes that sentence's certified answer non-unique; T6A0A, which names the right-hand edge, is fine.
